stories.notes: Wired the already-scored (1.00) recommend-intervention prompt into a trust-logged decision engine, mirroring STORY-012's predict-pressure orchestration pattern. Scoped as a thin wrapper: the engine accepts already-known decision parameters (icb_name, pressure_level, primary_driver, available_levers) as validated input rather than deriving them itself from raw GP PMS/NHS/ambulance/community data -- REQ-011 doesn't specify that derivation, and it's out of scope for this story's acceptance criteria. Found and corrected a real doc defect before starting: docs/stories/STORY-006.md said 'Blocked by: STORY-007' and STORY-007.md said 'Blocked by: STORY-006' -- a genuine circular dependency in the plan (also present in docs/STORIES.md), meaning neither story could ever start as literally written. Confirmed with the user this was a doc error, not a real constraint; corrected STORY-006.md's own line, left STORY-007.md untouched (out of scope for this story). Applied last story's drift-guard lesson from the start this time -- the recommend-intervention prompt copy matched the source .md file byte-for-byte on the first run, no transcription bug this time. Verified with 108 automated tests (tsc + node --test, all passing except one pre-existing unrelated skipped integration test) and one live, non-mocked call through makeDecision against the real Anthropic API, confirming a High-pressure/ambulance-driven scenario with divert_ambulances available correctly recommended divert_ambulances at high confidence.

criteria.text: Given operational data, when processed, then the dashboard displays current and forecasted metrics.
Given incomplete data, when processed, then the dashboard flags it for review.

stories.notes: Scoped as a backend-only data layer, confirmed with the user first: no frontend app or HTTP route exists anywhere in this repo yet, so a full UI + API in one story would not be a walking skeleton. buildDashboardSnapshot produces the data contract a future UI would render (current OPEL level + forecasted pressure_level per ICB, satisfying REQ-016) plus the already-scored draft-leadership-briefing output (REQ-012), with 'display activity' interpreted as each snapshot computation for trust-logging purposes. The task's own 'reuse' list named only STORY-002 and STORY-006, but neither produces a forecast -- used STORY-012's predict-pressure output for the forecasted metric instead, flagged to the user as an incomplete-citation situation matching STORY-012's own REQ-003/004 precedent. Incomplete/malformed ICB data is never hard-rejected -- it's flagged in a structured dataUncertainties list (no_icb_data, malformed_forecast:<icbName>) alongside the prompt's own fail-safe narrative handling, per this story's 'flag for review' criterion (distinct from STORY-006's 'reject bad input' criterion). Both prompt-drift-guard tests (recommend-intervention was already done; draft-leadership-briefing added here) passed byte-for-byte on the first run -- the STORY-012 lesson held. Verified with 120 automated tests and three live, non-mocked calls through buildDashboardSnapshot against the real Anthropic API (mixed-severity, empty-data, and malformed-tier scenarios) -- closing the gap that only the clear-case path had been proven live. FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-06, same session): built the previously-deferred frontend/HTTP layer. Backend: backend/src/app.ts (Express app factory) + backend/src/index.ts (entrypoint, SIGTERM-safe shutdown) + backend/src/routes/dashboardRoute.ts (POST /api/dashboard/snapshot -- Zod-validates request shape before any model call per CLAUDE.md's Contract Enforcement Layer, returns 200/snapshot on success, 502 for upstream/model failures, 500 for a trust-log write failure -- the one place 'fail loud' is intentionally absorbed since an HTTP handler is the trust boundary; supports an Idempotency-Key header for safe client retries, defaulting to a fresh UUID per request since each request is a new logical display event). Added supertest/@types/supertest as dev dependencies for route-level testing without hitting the real API. Frontend: scaffolded frontend/ with Vite + React + TS instead of the CLAUDE.md-documented CRA, confirmed with the user first and logged with reasoning in frontend/CLAUDE.md (CRA is deprecated upstream and heavy for a walking skeleton; same React+TS output, same folder conventions apply unchanged) -- only a booting placeholder page exists so far, no Dashboard page or backend integration yet. Verified: 128 backend tests (all passing except the one pre-existing unrelated skip), a real (non-supertest) server boot curled on a real port for both /health and /api/dashboard/snapshot (the latter against the real Anthropic API, correctly returning a Critical roll-up over HTTP), and a real frontend dev-server boot with the actual compiled App.tsx confirmed served (not a cached/stale page). Raises this story's confidence, since the literal 'the dashboard displays' wording now has a genuine (if minimal) UI + API surface behind it, though the Dashboard page itself still doesn't call the backend yet -- that remains the next real gap. FOLLOW-UP 2 (2026-09-06, same session): built the Dashboard page itself. frontend/src/services/dashboardApi.ts (fetchDashboardSnapshot -- explicit AbortController timeout per CLAUDE.md's external-call rule, returns a typed {outcome:'success'|'error'} result rather than throwing so the page can render an error state cleanly). frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx (three states: loading, error -- 'Dashboard loading error' -- and success, which renders briefing/metrics/dataUncertainties; entries are a required prop rather than self-fetched, since no backend endpoint assembles live ICB entries from ingestion yet -- App.tsx supplies hardcoded demo entries, explicitly flagged as a placeholder in a code comment). Added Vitest + React Testing Library + jsdom as dev dependencies (nothing existed before). Real bug found and fixed during BREAK/HARDEN: React Testing Library does not auto-unmount between tests under Vitest the way it does under Jest -- the second DashboardPage.test.tsx test failed with 'multiple elements found' because the previous test's alert role was still in the DOM. Fixed by adding an afterEach(cleanup) hook to frontend/src/setupTests.ts. Also found and fixed a real integration gap, not just a unit-test gap: fetchDashboardSnapshot uses a relative URL, but the Vite dev server and the backend run on different ports/origins, so a real browser fetch would have failed silently until deploy-time proxying was configured. Added a dev-only Vite proxy (server.proxy in vite.config.ts, /api -> http://localhost:3001) and verified it for real: booted both the actual backend and the actual Vite dev server, then curled the frontend's own origin at the exact path a browser fetch() would use (http://localhost:<vite-port>/api/dashboard/snapshot), confirming the request proxied through to the real backend and the real Anthropic API and returned a correct Critical roll-up. Production deployment still needs its own same-origin/reverse-proxy config (nginx) -- flagged in frontend/CLAUDE.md, not solved here. Verified: tsc -b --noEmit clean; 9 frontend tests (5 API client + 4 component) all passing after the cleanup fix; frontend production build succeeds; backend 128 tests unaffected (127 pass, 1 pre-existing skip). This closes the last named gap from the original STORY-007 confidence assessment -- the dashboard now genuinely displays fetched data end-to-end, not just a backend data contract.

stories.notes: Wired the already-scored (1.00, prompts/score-scenario-impact/v1.0.0.md) what-if prompt into a trust-logged simulator, mirroring STORY-006's decisionEngine.ts orchestration pattern exactly (validate -> render prompt -> call model with 5s timeout and capped retry -> trust-log every branch, success-path logging kept outside the model-call try block per the STORY-011/012/006 bug precedent). The one genuinely new design question -- what 'conflicting scenario inputs' (acceptance criterion 2) means, since nothing in the prompt's schema defines it -- was resolved by asking the user directly rather than assuming: a deterministic, code-side plausibility check (detectScenarioConflict in scenarioSimulatorTypes.ts) flags when current_pressure_level and current_primary_driver are mutually implausible (Low pressure with an active driver, or elevated pressure with driver 'none'). This is scoped narrowly to this simulator's own two fields, not the general uncertainty-flagging framework STORY-009 will build; it never blocks the projection, only surfaces alongside it as conflictFlags, matching dashboardSnapshot.ts's existing dataUncertainties pattern. The drift-guard test (scoreScenarioImpactPrompt.test.ts) was built from the start and passed byte-for-byte on the first run, same as STORY-006/007's guards. Verified with 142 automated tests (tsc --noEmit clean; 141/142 passing, 1 pre-existing unrelated skip) and two live, non-mocked calls through simulateScenario against the real Anthropic API: a clear-match case (High/ambulance_handover_delay/divert_ambulances) correctly projected Medium/Improves at 0.85 confidence, and a deliberately conflicting case (Low pressure with an active driver) was both flagged by the deterministic conflictFlags check and independently resolved by the model's own 'already at floor' rule -- proving criteria 1 and 2 against the real model path, not just the fake client. Trust log verifyIntegrity() reported valid across both real-call entries. The task brief's framing that the workspace repo was 'not provisioned yet' was false on inspection (docs/stories/STORY-008.md and this progress.json entry already existed) -- surfaced to the user before starting, same as the STORY-012/STORY-006 precedent for stale framing. FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-13, same day): the original demo only live-tested 2 of the prompt's 5 documented scenario categories (clear-match, conflict) through simulateScenario itself -- the other 3 (general-purpose lever, mismatched scenario, already-at-floor) were only proven via the fake client and the standalone prompt eval. Ran 3 more live, non-mocked calls: Medium/discharge_delay/call_in_additional_staff correctly projected Low/Improves at 0.55 confidence (general-purpose, lower-confidence rule); High/critical_care_occupancy/divert_ambulances correctly projected High/No change at 0.7 confidence (mismatched-scenario rule); Low/none/open_surge_beds correctly projected Low/No change at 0.9 confidence (already-at-floor rule). All three matched the prompt's documented rules exactly. Trust log verifyIntegrity() reported valid across all 3 new entries. This closes the confidence gap named in the original completion report -- all 5 of score-scenario-impact's documented scenario categories are now proven live through this story's actual code path, not just the eval script. NOTE (2026-09-13, during rebase): a Colaberry Build Bot sync commit (66f3f53) landed on origin/main between this session's two pushes and reset this story's (and several others') passed/files_touched/notes fields to blank, contradicting docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md's stated contract that a sync preserves Claude-owned passed flags and notes. Restored this story's own fields during the rebase per the user's explicit instruction; other stories' reset fields were deliberately left as the bot set them, not this session's call to make -- flagged to the user rather than silently fixed.

criteria.text: Given uncertain data, when detected, then the system flags it for human review.
Given certain data, when processed, then the system does not flag it.
Trust: The system logs all flagging activities and ensures human review.

stories.notes: Built as deterministic code, not an LLM call, per the user's explicit choice (this story's own confidence question): prompts/flag-data-uncertainty/v1.1.0.md already specifies the exact 5-category decision tree (conflicting_sources > malformed_input > missing_value > stale_data > none) and has 5 user-confirmed eval cases, but only ever scored 0.60 in eval -- well below this library's 0.85 ready bar -- and every other uncertainty-flag mechanism already in this codebase (generateInsights.ts, generateNhsInsights.ts, dashboardSnapshot.ts, detectScenarioConflict) is deterministic, none call an LLM. detectDataUncertainty.ts ports the prompt's exact category rules and ranges into pure TypeScript, matching all 5 confirmed eval cases exactly (100% vs the prompt's 60%) plus 5 additional boundary/false-positive tests. flagForReview.ts orchestrates it: validates input via Zod (invalid_input, no detector call -- cleanest form of the 'flagging mechanism failure' failure path), runs the detector under a timeout budget ('data processing delay'), and is fail-safe rather than fail-loud on an internal detector exception or timeout -- flags the record for review rather than silently passing it, same philosophy as classify-metric-status's 'default to the most severe status, never a falsely-calm one.' Trust-logs every branch via the existing FileTrustLogger (reused, not rebuilt -- processType 'prediction', since trustSpine/types.ts's enum is a file outside this story's scope and 'prediction' already covers non-ingestion determinations like the decision engine and simulator). A trust-log write failure is the one place this still fails loud (throws), matching every prior story's precedent. Flagged and corrected a stale framing in the task brief before starting: it listed STORY-011 (the trust spine) as 'coming next, do not build' when it already exists and was reused here, same pattern as STORY-006/008's stale-framing flags. Caught and fixed one test-design bug during BREAK/HARDEN before it shipped: the first timeout test used a synchronous busy-wait to simulate a slow detector, which cannot actually be preempted by the timeout race (JS's single-threaded scheduling means a synchronous block cannot yield to a concurrently-running timer) -- widened DataUncertaintyDetector's type to allow an async return and rewrote the test with a real setTimeout-based delay, which the timeout race then correctly preempted (confirmed by the test's own ~35ms duration against a 20ms budget and a 50ms detector delay). FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-13, same day): closed the confidence gap that nothing in the codebase actually called flagForReview yet. Added fromGpPmsCapacityRecord() (backend/src/services/uncertaintyFlagging/fromGpPmsRecord.ts), a read-only adapter mapping a real STORY-001 GpPmsRecord into the DataRecord shape -- additive only, gpPms/generateInsights.ts's own working dataUncertainties logic was left completely untouched rather than risking already-shipped, tested code. Proved the mechanism against genuine pipeline data, not just hand-built fixtures: fetched real records via the real MockGpPmsClient, mapped the capacity record, and ran it through flagForReview twice -- once evaluated shortly after its own capturedAt (correctly not flagged) and once evaluated at the real current system time (correctly flagged stale_data, since the fixture's fixed 2026-08-22 timestamp is genuinely ~3 weeks old by now, not a fabricated scenario). A final live demo ran the same chain end-to-end against the real FileTrustLogger (not the fake), confirming valid trust-log integrity. FOLLOW-UP 2 (2026-09-13, same day): extended the same read-only adapter pattern to the remaining 3 real pipelines. fromNhsCentralDataRecord.ts maps any one of an NhsCentralDataRecord's 4 typed metrics (opelLevel, ambulanceHandoverOver60MinPct, dischargeDelayBeddays, criticalCareOccupancyPct); fromAmbulanceHandoverRecord.ts and fromCommunityDischargeRecord.ts map their single typed numeric field each. All three, like fromGpPmsRecord.ts, are additive-only -- nhsCentralData/ambulance/community's own shipped, tested ingestion and insight-generation files are untouched. Proved each against real (not fabricated) data: the NHS adapter was verified twice, once against FakeNhsCentralDataClient's fixtures (the automated test) and once against a live call through the real McpNhsCentralDataClient spawning the actual nhs-ops-status subprocess (a throwaway demo, deleted after, matching STORY-002/012's precedent for real-subprocess verification); the ambulance and community adapters were verified against their real MockAmbulanceClient/MockCommunityClient fixtures. Every adapter was checked both fresh (not flagged) and at the real current system clock (genuinely stale, since every fixture's timestamp is now weeks old) -- not a single fabricated staleness scenario across any of the four pipelines. FOLLOW-UP 3 (2026-09-13, same day, user explicitly requested wiring it in automatically after being asked to confirm the scope): wired the mechanism into all 4 pipelines' own analyze*/generateInsights functions, not just standalone adapters. Called detectDataUncertainty directly rather than the full flagForReview() orchestrator -- flagForReview's own trust-log write would have doubled each function's 'logged exactly once' trust-spine contract (3 tests per pipeline assert this), a real regression caught immediately by running each pipeline's own test suite after the change, exactly as planned when asking for confirmation. GP PMS (generateInsights.ts) and NHS (generateNhsInsights.ts) check the capacity/per-ICB records respectively, matching the story's own confirmed design. Ambulance and community needed a genuinely different design, not just a threshold tweak: they are historical event logs (many past occurrences), unlike GP PMS's live capacity snapshot or NHS's per-ICB current-state records, so flagging every individual past event as 'stale' mismatched the mechanism's intent and broke 2 real integration tests (analyzeAmbulanceData.test.ts, analyzeCommunityData.test.ts) that use the real mock clients' older fixture records against a fixed now. Fixed by checking only the most-recent record per batch, mirroring the existing stale_data check's own semantics, rather than looping over every record. All 4 integrations are additive to the existing dataUncertainties array (new tag prefixes: capacity_metric_uncertain:, icb_metric_uncertain:<icbName>:, most_recent_handover_uncertain:, most_recent_discharge_uncertain:) -- none of the 4 modules' existing checks, output shapes, or tests were removed or restructured. FOLLOW-UP 4 (2026-09-13, same day): closed the two remaining confidence-report caveats. (1) The value < 0 implausibility heuristic: verified, not just assumed, against every metric actually wired into this system -- opelLevel, ambulanceHandoverOver60MinPct, dischargeDelayBeddays, criticalCareOccupancyPct, handoverDurationMinutes, and delayedDischargeBedDays all already carry a schema-level non-negative bound in their own *RecordSchema, so a negative value for any of them is rejected before ever reaching detectDataUncertainty; only GP PMS's unbounded booked_slots_today/available_slots_today can arrive negative, where it's unambiguously implausible. Updated the code comment to state this as verified fact, not an open assumption -- no code change needed, since no current metric contradicts the rule. (2) Reviewed the confidence-score formulas' actual output across representative inputs per category with the user directly (mirroring how eval.jsonl's original values were confirmed) rather than only self-certifying the tolerance match. Found and fixed one real issue in the process: the 'none' category's formula (1.0 - 0.1*ratio, clamped to 0.90) hit its floor at ratio=1 and stayed flat at 0.90 all the way to ratio=3, not differentiating 'barely on schedule' from 'almost due' within the healthy range. Rescaled to decrease linearly across the whole not-yet-stale window (1.0 - (0.1/3)*ratio) per the user's confirmed choice -- now smoothly 1.00 at ratio=0 down to 0.90 at ratio=3, still matching the prompt's declared 0.90-1.00 range and still within tolerance of the one confirmed eval case for this category (0.99 vs the eval's 0.97, diff 0.02). stale_data/missing_value/conflicting_sources/malformed_input curves were reviewed and confirmed as-is, no changes.

stories.notes: Ambulance and community ingestion (REQ-003/004) built from scratch mirroring the GP PMS pattern (injectable client interface + fixture-backed mock, no real credentials exist for either system). AI intelligence layer wires the existing predict-pressure prompt (scored 1.00, previously unwired) to live ambulance/community insights plus an NHS central data record via a new @anthropic-ai/sdk dependency. Verified with 95 automated tests (tsc + node --test, all passing except one pre-existing skipped integration test), one live, non-mocked call through analyzeIcbPressure against the real Anthropic API confirming the model genuinely used the live ambulance/community feeds over the NHS record's own bundled numbers, and a second live call confirming a genuine API auth rejection is correctly classified as AuthError. Found and fixed two real bugs during BREAK/HARDEN: (1) predictPressure.ts's success-path trust-log call was originally inside the same try block as the model call, so a simulated trust-log write failure was misclassified as a retryable model error instead of propagating -- the same bug class STORY-011 hit in the ingestion pipelines; (2) predictPressurePrompt.ts's hand-copied template had silently dropped backtick formatting present in the actual scored prompts/predict-pressure/v1.0.0.md, caught by a new drift-guard test that compares the rendered prompt byte-for-byte against the source file. User explicitly confirmed (asked directly, not assumed) that partial ambulance/community data should be passed to predict-pressure as null fields rather than treated as no_data -- matches the shipped behavior.
